item.title: Cloudflare launches Search for Agents to enable AI-powered site search
item.description:
Cloudflare launches Search for Agents to enable AI-powered site search

Cloudflare today introduced Search for Agents, a new toggle in the Cloudflare dashboard that creates an AI Search instance for a zone, indexes its content, and makes the search API available from the customer’s own domain.

🔍 Overview

  • Search for Agents is activated via a toggle in the Cloudflare dashboard.
  • It is available to all customers, including the Free plan (with limits).
  • Enabling the feature causes Cloudflare to create an AI Search instance, start indexing the zone’s content, and expose a searchable endpoint under the customer’s domain.

🧩 How it works

  • The feature can be turned on from the Quick Actions section of the zone page or via the API.
  • Once enabled, Cloudflare automatically creates the AI Search instance with default settings and begins crawling the site.
  • The search endpoint is advertised on every page of the site to facilitate discoverability.
  • If Markdown for Agents is also enabled, a request with Accept: text/markdown returns the same information in YAML front‑matter, allowing agents to pick up instructions easily.
  • Depending on the AI Search configuration, agents may query the endpoint using natural‑language questions.

⚙️ Configuration

  • The default AI Search instance can be re‑configured at any time, such as enabling reranking or changing cache settings.
  • Search usage is subject to the zone’s domain settings, including bot‑management rules, AI Crawl Control, and Web Application Firewall configurations.

🚀 Availability

  • Search for Agents can be enabled through the dashboard toggle or programmatically via the API.
  • The feature is offered to all customers, including those on the Free tier, though the Free tier operates under unspecified limits.

💡 Benefits

  • Provides a network‑level AI search API that any agent can discover and use without manual index setup.
  • Keeps search functionality under the customer’s own domain, preserving control over security and traffic policies.
  • Reduces operational overhead by automatically handling crawling, indexing, and endpoint advertisement.

#Cloudflare #SearchForAgents #AIsearch

Source: Introducing Search for Agents

item.title: Cloudflare Builds DNS Testing Tool Using Flamingo Framework
item.description:
Cloudflare Builds DNS Testing Tool Using Flamingo Framework

🔍 Overview

After a DNS service rollout, unit tests passed and dashboards showed green, but production suddenly broke. Some record changes sat unpublished for hours due to a scheduling bug, causing slow hostname resolution and certificate issuance delays. DNS failures are hard to catch because they are slow, spread across the network, and only partially impact where they cause problems.

🧩 How it works

The Cloudflare DNS team extended Flamingo, their end-to-end testing framework, to test DNS the way customers experience it: constantly, from every data center, and against production. Flamingo’s modular design lets teams add support for other networking protocols. Originally built around complex multi-step HTTP testing, its capabilities have increased substantially over the years.

⚙️ Key details

Flamingo is built from the ground up with Cloudflare’s infrastructure in mind:

  • Built a control plane and scheduler that let teams target specific environments, data centers, or percentages of metals
  • Integrates with custom reporting, metrics, and analytics tooling
  • Needs predictable performance and runs well on bare-metal servers in resource-constrained environments
  • Uses a custom domain-specific language (DSL) consisting of a simple setup-request-response format
  • Written in Rust due to its consistent performance characteristics and strong type system
  • The type system enables modularity through strongly-typed enumerations for input and output in the action runner

With just five lines of code, a script can run anywhere on Cloudflare’s edge and scale to thousands of requests per minute. The data from millions of data points is turned into a graph defining how the service is actually performing in the real world.

Component Description
Control plane and scheduler Let teams target specific environments, data centers, or percentages of metals
DSL Uses simple setup-request-response format, only 5 lines of code for scalable testing
Rust Provides consistent performance and strong type system for modularity

💡 Why it matters

Unit testing alone is not enough for complex network pathways with multiple systems. We need to run constant automated testing against real systems and measure outcomes to make informed decisions on service health. Flamingo measures the behavior of production environments to ensure lower-tier code behaves as expected. The DNS measurements now decide whether a release goes ahead or gets rolled back.

#DNS #Testing #Infrastructure #Cloudflare

Source: Probing DNS at Cloudflare

item.title: Critical phpAfterShell Vulnerability Disclosed in PHP Session Handler
item.description:
Critical phpAfterShell Vulnerability Disclosed in PHP Session Handler

On November 19, 2026, the security research company depthfirst disclosed phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714), a critical vulnerability in PHP’s default file-based session handler that can lead to remote code execution. PHP released official patches to resolve this and 16 other security vulnerabilities on the same day. There is currently no indication that these vulnerabilities have been exploited in the wild.

🔍 Overview

Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, phpAfterShell scores a 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The PHP project addressed the flaw in versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, and 8.6.0. These releases also resolve 16 other security vulnerabilities, six of which are similarly rated as critical.

As of November 19, 2026, none of the 17 vulnerabilities are listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and no reviewed sources report active exploitation.

🧩 How it works

PHP stores session data in files by default. The phpAfterShell vulnerability involves the session write and deserialization processes:

  • Session read: When an application calls session_start(), PHP reads the session file and deserializes its content into the $_SESSION array.
  • Session write: When the request ends, PHP writes the updated session back to the same file.
  • Interruption: phpAfterShell is triggered when this write operation is interrupted. Following an interruption, the session file can hold the beginning of the new session data followed by the leftover end of the old session data.
  • Deserialization: On the next request, session_start() deserializes this mixed content. If an attacker managed to shape the old session data, PHP can deserialize objects of the attacker’s choosing.

An attacker can shape the stored session data by using PHP’s session upload progress feature (which writes file upload progress into the session) or by targeting applications that store large user-controlled strings in the session. Although PHP notes that code execution requires a write interruption at a useful point and a suitable deserialization gadget chain in the application, depthfirst reports reaching code execution without any application gadget. They achieved this by chaining phpAfterShell with a second, undisclosed memory-corruption bug in a PHP-native class. It is unestablished whether this second bug is fixed in the November 19 releases.

⚙️ Mitigation and Protection

To mitigate the vulnerability, Cloudflare has updated its Web Application Firewall (WAF) to block known phpAfterShell attack patterns. These updates build on a PHP remote code execution rule first deployed in October 2026 for the php2shell vulnerabilities, which has now been updated to cover phpAfterShell.

Rule Name / Feature Target Vulnerability Managed Ruleset Default Action
phpAfterShell Rule CVE-2026-126714 Free and Paid (Enabled by default) Block
PHP-FPM Request Smuggling Rule CVE-2026-129289 Paid Plans (Enabled by default) Log
PHP SOAP Extension Rules CVE-2026-15353, CVE-2026-129506 Paid Plans (Enabled by default) Log

The request smuggling and SOAP rules use the “Log” action by default because the traffic patterns they target can occasionally occur in legitimate traffic. Paid plan customers can review matching requests in Security Events and change the action to “Block” once they verify that legitimate traffic is unaffected.

Cloudflare emphasizes that the WAF serves as an additional layer of defense rather than a complete replacement for patching. Because several of the critical flaws depend on server configuration or bypass pathways visible to the WAF, the only complete fix is to upgrade PHP and restart all worker processes.

#PHP #phpAfterShell #Cybersecurity #Cloudflare #Vulnerability

Source: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws

item.title: 2026 U.S. Election Websites See Traffic Surge, Minimal DDoS Activity
item.description:
2026 U.S. Election Websites See Traffic Surge, Minimal DDoS Activity

Visitors to U.S. government election websites surged 363% on November 3, 2026, the day of the midterm elections, while Cloudflare recorded no major DDoS attacks on protected sites.

🔍 Overview

  • Traffic to state and local election websites reached about 602 million requests on Election Day, up from 130 million on November 1.
  • Overall traffic across Cloudflare’s global network rose only 12% during the same period.
  • Attacks focused on gaining access to internal systems and data rather than taking sites offline.
  • Major DDoS activity was absent on Election Day; only one significant DDoS occurred on November 2 targeting a California House candidate with 520,000 requests.

⚙️ Key details

  • Website vulnerability attempts were 180 times more frequent than DDoS attacks and ten times the rate seen across Cloudflare’s broader customer base.
  • Vulnerability exploit attempts rose from 200,000 per day in January to 2 million per day in October.
  • In the 12 months before the election, Cloudflare mitigated 392 million website vulnerability attacks on government election websites.
  • Cross‑site scripting attacks inject malicious code into web pages to capture administrator credentials or deface site content.
  • SQL injection manipulates database queries to potentially extract voter records or alter data.
    Attack Type Description
    Cross‑site scripting Injects malicious code into web pages to capture admin credentials or deface content
    SQL injection Manipulates database queries to potentially extract voter records or alter data

🚀 Availability

  • No escalation in attack volume and zero major DDoS incidents were detected across the 1,400 protected election-related websites on Election Day.
  • The only significant DDoS attack occurred on November 2, targeting a California U.S. House candidate and totaling 520,000 requests.
  • Traffic to state and local election websites was higher on Election Day than any other day in 2026, reaching approximately 602 million requests.
  • By contrast, traffic across the rest of Cloudflare’s network increased only 12% over the same period.

💡 Why it matters

  • Cloudflare’s free election protection programs (Athenian Project, Cloudflare for Campaigns, Project Galileo) helped protect more than 1,400 election‑related websites belonging to governments, candidates, parties, advocates, journalists and civil‑society groups.
  • Cloudflare launched its first election protection program in 2016 after widespread reports of cyberattacks targeting the U.S. elections.
  • Despite the surge in traffic and increased vulnerability attempts, cyberattacks did not disrupt the 2026 election, underscoring the effectiveness of the protective measures.

#Election #Cybersecurity #Cloudflare #DDoS #Vulnerability

Source: Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections

item.title: Cloudflare Updates Clairic Extraction Model and Introduces Lighter Clairic-flash Variant
item.description:
Cloudflare Updates Clairic Extraction Model and Introduces Lighter Clairic-flash Variant

Cloudflare’s Workers AI superintelligence team has announced a major update to Clairic, its frontier AI extraction model, alongside the release of a lighter, faster 9-billion-parameter model called Clairic-flash. Based on feedback from its preview release, Cloudflare redesigned the architecture of Clairic to improve extraction accuracy from complex documents, including images and multi-page PDFs, while maintaining fast performance and open-weights availability on Hugging Face.

🔍 Overview

Cloudflare has transitioned into a neolab building its own frontier AI models for customers and the open-source community. Since announcing the preview of Clairic, the team received extensive feedback on customer use cases, such as extracting data from images of receipts and reading values from support tickets. To excel at reading from unstructured data, the team redesigned the model’s architecture to prioritize highly accurate data extraction.

🧩 How it works

The new architecture introduces several updates to improve extraction performance:

  • Parallel Slot Autoregressive Generation: Instead of a single forward pass, the model now uses parallel slot autoregressive generation for ordinary text and number extraction fields. Each field uses its already written tokens to select the next token and stops at its own end marker. This parallel advancement occurs in the serving batch to ensure fast latency.
  • Specialized Heads: Trained specialized heads handle computation, estimation, forecasts, durations, calculated dates, and explicit arithmetic.
  • Preserved API Features: Despite the architectural changes, the typed API interface still provides confidence scores, character spans, and probabilities with every request.

⚙️ Key details

The updated models offer significant functional improvements over the preview version:

  • Multi-Page and Document Support: The models now support reading complex documents, including PDFs and up to four total images or PDF pages. In a single request, users can extract information such as the supplier, total, and line items (which return as rows preserving the association of description, quantity, and price).
  • Improved Accuracy: On internal benchmarks covering text and images, image reading accuracy improved from 207 errors to 0.
  • Sub-Second Latency: Latency tests measuring complete HTTP responses from self-hosted servers demonstrate response times under one second.

🚀 Availability

Both models are hosted on Workers AI, and their full open weights are available on Hugging Face.

Model Parameter Count Workers AI Endpoint Pricing (per Million Input Tokens)
Clairic 27B @cf/cloudflare/clairic $0.24
Clairic-flash 9B @cf/cloudflare/clairic-flash $0.10

Clairic’s pricing follows System One pricing principles, meaning users are only charged for input tokens, and Cloudflare covers the cost of output token generation.

#Cloudflare #WorkersAI #Clairic #LLM #DataExtraction

Source: An updated Clairic and Clairic-flash are now open-weight, from the new Workers AI Superintelligence team

item.title: Quad9 Withdraws Public DNS Resolver from France Following Court Ruling
item.description:
Quad9 Withdraws Public DNS Resolver from France Following Court Ruling

Last month, the Swiss non-profit foundation Quad9 announced that it will withdraw its free public DNS resolver from France. This decision followed months of litigation and a French court ruling that imposed daily financial penalties on Quad9 for failing to block domains associated with alleged copyright infringement.

🔍 Overview

The French court’s ruling forced Quad9 to choose between crippling litigation and financial penalties, or fundamentally altering its service in a way that would undermine the privacy and security of its users. Left with no good option, Quad9 is choosing to withdraw its service. This withdrawal deprives French Internet users of a trustworthy tool and creates a real risk of disruption to their daily lives.

🧩 How it works

DNS resolvers are a foundational piece of the Internet’s infrastructure.

  • Address Translation: When a user types a website name, the DNS system translates that domain name into the IP address the device needs to connect.
  • Resolution: A DNS resolver looks up that address and sends it back to the device, functioning like an operator finding a phone number in a directory.
  • Blocking Limitations: The only way a DNS resolver can block content is by declining to return the IP address for a particular website. It cannot remove the actual infringing content from the Internet, nor can it take down the servers hosting it.

⚙️ Key details

Multiple public DNS resolvers are utilized globally, but they are increasingly facing regional legal pressures:

Resolver Name Provider Details
9.9.9.9 Quad9 Withdrawing from France; used by government bodies, educational institutions, hospitals, and utilities.
1.1.1.1 Cloudflare Launched in April 2018 as a fast, reliable, privacy-first consumer DNS service that does not collect or sell user data.
8.8.8.8 Google One of the best-known public resolvers.
OpenDNS Cisco Previously withdrawn from France, Portugal, and Belgium (temporarily) under similar circumstances.

💡 Why it matters

If affected parties in France do not change their resolver before Quad9 removes its service, their Internet will fail with no explanation. Quad9 has no way to directly notify these users that their resolver will soon stop working.

This challenge is part of a broader trend. A Belgian court recently issued an order that would impose substantial penalties if Cloudflare, Google, and Cisco do not begin blocking websites through their public resolvers by early January 2027. Cloudflare, which has spent years advocating against orders of this kind, has raised concerns that unrelenting demands for blocking by public DNS resolvers will end up causing real harm to the Internet.

#DNS #InternetInfrastructure #Quad9 #Cloudflare #InternetPrivacy

Source: Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine

item.title: Cloudflare Launches Two System One AI Models
item.description:
Cloudflare Launches Two System One AI Models

Cloudflare announced it is turning its AI platform into a neolab and unveiled two new System One models, Clef and Clairic.

🔍 Overview

  • Cloudflare has been essential web infrastructure for the past decade and a half.
  • It is now positioning itself as a neolab, per a presentation at the AI Engineer Code Summit by Michelle Chen, who runs Cloudflare’s AI Platform on the product side.
  • The company claims to be a neolab because it has begun launching models.
  • Two System One models were introduced: Clef and Clairic.
  • The term neolab was coined in November by Stephanie Palazzolo and defined as a new generation of research‑focused AI startups.
  • Cloudflare does not meet at least half of the neolab criteria because it is a public company with significant revenue.

🧩 How it works

  • Clef is a decision model directly inspired by TypeSafe AI’s Jev model.
  • Clairic is an extract model that can take unstructured input and extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values in one forward pass.
  • System One models enable work to be done by smaller, faster models with output measured in milliseconds rather than seconds.
  • Post‑training is the primary focus of Cloudflare’s model development team.

⚙️ Key details

  • Record earnings: annualized revenue crossed $3 billion and quarterly revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year.
  • CEO Matthew Prince called the third quarter Cloudflare’s best ever.
  • Jev’s September arrival was described as “the east wind” that reshaped Cloudflare’s AI model perspective.
  • Clef was built in two weeks, a copy of Jev; TypeSafe AI spent two years developing Jev.
  • TypeSafe is credited with creating the Jev model and providing the API schema Cloudflare uses.
  • Cloudflare’s AI Platform team concentrates on post‑training.

💡 Why it matters

  • System One models let smaller, faster models perform work measured in milliseconds, improving efficiency.
  • Clairic can extract typed values such as order numbers from unstructured data like invoices, reducing LLM error risk.
  • The approach allows Cloudflare to handle some requests without sending them to a large language model, potentially lowering latency and cost.
  • Post‑training is the main development focus, suggesting efficiency gains from refining existing models rather than building new ones.
  • Cloudflare’s public status and revenue indicate it is not a typical neolab, but its AI platform expansion signals a strategic shift toward research‑focused capabilities.

#Cloudflare #AI #SystemOne #PostTraining

Source: Cloudflare Joins the Jevolution and Labels Itself a Neolab — Latent Space

item.title: AI agents face expanding blocks across major web services
item.description:
AI agents face expanding blocks across major web services

A wave of website restrictions is limiting the ability of autonomous AI agents—promised by OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct and others—to act on users’ behalf across the internet.

🔍 Overview

  • “Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI.”
  • Companies market agents that can “scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.”
  • In recent weeks, users report blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks on top websites.

🤖 Agents Mentioned

  • Meta’s Muse
  • xAI’s Grok
  • OpenAI’s Dots
  • Instinct’s AI agent
  • Perplexity’s shopping agent

🛡️ Companies Blocking AI Agents

Company Action
Yelp Allows only AI agents that pay for its data licensing program
Delta Air Lines Preventing agents from booking tickets
JPMorgan Chase Blocking agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns
Charles Schwab Blocking agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns
Cars.com No longer accessible to agents
Amtrak No longer accessible to agents
Amazon Banned Perplexity’s agentic shopping feature and is blocking Muse, Grok, Instinct agents, and OpenAI’s Dots
Google (reports on Reddit) Blocking some accounts that use Muse due to “suspicious activity”
Walmart (reports) Issues checking out for agents despite Meta partnership
Cloudflare Introduced a one‑click block for AI crawlers in 2025 and now blocks crawlers that scrape for both search indexing and AI training

⚖️ Legal Tussles with Amazon

  • “Amazon was already fighting off AI agents last year when it banned Perplexity’s agentic shopping feature and sued the AI startup.”
  • Amazon claimed it “repeatedly requested” Perplexity stop allowing its agents to shop on its website.
  • Perplexity argued Amazon doesn’t want agents because it “won’t get as many human eyeballs in front of its ads.”
  • A judge ordered Perplexity to stop its agents on Amazon, but an appeals court overturned the ruling in August.
  • Amazon has since filed an amended complaint.

🤝 Responses & Workarounds

  • Meta said, “Turning away a personal agent means turning away the customer behind it,” and prefers to work with businesses rather than lose customers.
  • Meta partnered with retailers such as Walmart, Gap, Sephora, Best Buy and others to allow Muse to shop on their sites.
  • Shopify opened its network of storefronts to AI agents.
  • Meta responded to instances of websites blocking Muse in a post earlier this month.

🌐 Infrastructure Measures

  • Cloudflare’s one‑click block aims to “save the web from an influx of AI bots, which is putting a strain on internet infrastructure and wrecking email inboxes.”
  • Canal notes that these blocks may make the web more “annoying” as more sites add human‑verification steps, potentially affecting even simple grocery‑shopping sites.

#AIagents #WebBlocking #AutonomousAgents #Ecommerce #Cloudflare

Source: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents

item.title: Cloudflare Acquires Deno, Announces End of Deno Runtime Support
item.description:
Cloudflare Acquires Deno, Announces End of Deno Runtime Support

On 9 October 2026 Cloudflare announced it has acquired Deno.

🔍 Overview

  • The Deno team released the first version of celld in August, an open‑source implementation of the Durable Objects pattern from Cloudflare Workers.
  • Cloudflare’s acquisition aims to build on celld to “make workerd self‑hosting a first‑class supported way to build and run apps using the Workers programming model.”

⚙️ Key Details

  • Cloudflare will support the Deno runtime for another year with monthly releases containing bug fixes and security updates.
  • After that year Cloudflare will end its development of the Deno runtime.
  • Deno will remain open source, and others are welcomed to continue its development.

🗣️ Statements from the Deno Creator

  • “It’s a joint decision and I agree with it.”
  • “I’m most invested in its success and have put the most work into it – and I no longer think it’s where I can do the most important work.”
  • “There are some good ideas in Deno and it’s well engineered – but it ultimately is not solving big problems.”
  • “It has been sucked into the gravity well of node compatibility, which forces it to behave exactly as Node does.”
  • “Why reimplement Node? It works. Marginal performance or UX or security benefits are not enough. I’m interested in building powerful new abstractions.”

🧩 celld and the Workers Model

  • celld works remarkably well, depending only on object storage for coordination and persistence.
  • It is described as an entirely new model for server development, not just a slightly different API to interact with the file system or network.

🔐 Permissions System Comparison

Platform Permissions model available Network host allow‑listing
Deno Fine‑grained allow‑list for files, folders, and network hosts Supported
Node.js Permissions added in v20.0.0 (April 2023) and stable in v22.13.0 (Jan 2025) Not supported (network is either on or off)

📅 Recent Related Articles (dates)

  • “A new feature for my blog, built using my voice” – 9 Oct 2026
  • “Claude Haiku 5.5” – 7 Oct 2026
  • “We’re going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything” – 3 Oct 2026
  • “OpenAI DevDay 2026 live blog” – 29 Sep 2026

#Deno #Cloudflare #Serverless #OpenSource

Source: Deno is joining Cloudflare

item.title: Cloudflare and Strands Release Open Decision Models for AI Agents
item.description:
Cloudflare and Strands Release Open Decision Models for AI Agents

Cloudflare and Strands Labs released open-source decision models and RL fine-tuning tools designed to help AI agents make fast, structured choices efficiently.

🔍 Overview

Two new open-source “decision” models were released this week, along with supporting services, aimed at replacing expensive, general-purpose LLM calls for routine agent tasks. Cloudflare shipped Clef and Clef‑flash, and Strands Labs published Strands Decider 2B.

🧩 How it works

Decision models are optimized to return structured choices (not freeform text), such as routing a ticket, deciding to escalate, or approving/denying an action. They operate with lower latency and cost than calling a full LLM, making them useful for agent routing, guardrails, and tool selection.

⚙️ Key details

  • Clef and Clef‑flash (Cloudflare): Open-source models with Apache‑2.0 license. Cloudflare added an RL fine‑tuning service for them on Workers AI.
  • Strands Decider 2B (Strands Labs): A 2‑billion parameter open-source model with weights and training scripts published, designed to run locally and return confidence‑scored choices in tens to low hundreds of milliseconds.

💡 Why it matters

  • Decision models let agents make cheap, fast, and calibrated choices with lower latency and cost than calling a full LLM.
  • Small, calibrated decision models make it practical to offload routine, high‑volume decisions from expensive LLM calls — lowering cost and making agent tool calls safer by verifying arguments or gating premature actions.
  • Clef’s Apache‑2.0 weights and Worker hosting affect on‑prem versus cloud tradeoffs.
  • For teams building agents, moving routine classification or tool‑selection logic to a decision model can cut latency and infer costs.

#Cloudflare #StrandsLabs #DecisionModels #AIAgents #OpenSource #RLAIF

Source: AI Agent News Today — October 2, 2026 Source: 13 Best AI Web App Builders in 2026: Tested and Compared

item.title: Cloudflare Reports AI Bots Exceed Half of Web Traffic, Adjusts Controls
item.description:
Cloudflare Reports AI Bots Exceed Half of Web Traffic, Adjusts Controls

Cloudflare announced that, as of June, bots account for more than half of all internet traffic. The surge is linked to AI companies scraping the web and AI agents acting on behalf of users. In response, the company is expanding its traffic‑control options for site owners.

🔍 Overview

  • Cloudflare found in June that bots made up more than half of internet traffic.
  • The proportion is rising as AI companies and AI agents increase their activity online.
  • Cloudflare positions itself between websites and those agents, offering owners granular control.

📈 AI Traffic Impact

  • Bots include both malicious scrapers and legitimate AI tools.
  • Site owners can block all AI tools, allow all, or allow only those that might pay for access.
  • AI is also “upending everything inside of Cloudflare.”

🛡️ Cloudflare’s Controls

  • The network spans over 350 cities worldwide and thousands of data centers.
  • Services aim to keep applications and content safe and fast.
  • Matthew Prince has described Cloudflare as “a service that makes the internet faster and protects it from bad guys.”

⚙️ Internal AI Changes

  • Earlier this year Cloudflare laid off more than a thousand people, about 20 % of its workforce.
  • Matthew Prince wrote an op‑ed in the Wall Street Journal titled “How I choose which Cloudflare employees to replace with AI.”

💡 Why It Matters

  • The shift in traffic composition forces a rethink of the internet’s business model, which has been dominated by advertising for the past 30 years, largely shaped by Google.
  • Cloudflare is exploring how to shape a healthier future business model for the internet while managing the growing influence of non‑human traffic.

🗣️ Public Discussion

  • At Web Summit, Prince was asked when non‑human traffic might surpass human traffic online, highlighting industry curiosity about the trajectory of AI‑driven web activity.

#Cloudflare #AItraffic #Bots #InternetInfrastructure

Source: Cloudflare’s mission to save the web from AI… with AI

item.title: Cloudflare Python Workers Reach General Availability
item.description:
Cloudflare Python Workers Reach General Availability

Cloudflare has announced that support for running Python code on its server-side Workers platform is now generally available following a two-year preview period.

💡 Why it matters

Cloudflare states that “Python is now a first-class, fully supported language on the Cloudflare Developer Platform.” This release represents a significant investment in the Python ecosystem.

⚙️ Key details

Cloudflare achieves this functionality by running Python compiled to WebAssembly via Pyodide within its V8-based workerd runtime. Notable limitations include:

  • Multiprocessing is non-functional in the WebAssembly VM.
  • Threading is non-functional in the WebAssembly VM.

🛠️ Development Tools

Developers can utilize the pywrangler tool (packaged as workers-py on PyPI) to run a full local simulation of the Cloudflare stack. This tool executes code using Pyodide in WebAssembly within a 123MB workerd binary.

👥 Credits

The release announcement is credited to Gyeongjae Choi, Dominik Picheta, and Hood Chatham, with Gyeongjae Choi and Hood Chatham identified as Pyodide core maintainers.

#Cloudflare #Python #WebAssembly #Pyodide #Serverless

Source: Cloudflare Python Workers are now generally available
